_doc: The example household's own facts - the things a statement cannot carry.
Statements say what was bought, sold and held. They do not say whether a
household files jointly, which state taxes it, or what the rest of its
income is - and every tax threshold turns on the first, the state figure
on the second, and where a gain lands on the third. So the demo seeds
these, or it can answer 'what do I own' and nothing about what it costs.
WHY THIS FILE RATHER THAN CONSTANTS ON EITHER SIDE. The generator builds
statements around these numbers and asserts the lessons still land; Orby
reads the same file to seed the project's profile. Two copies would drift,
and the failure would be quiet: the household would still look plausible
while the headroom the onboarding copy quotes stopped being true.
INVENTED, like everything else here. The project carrying this profile is
marked as an example, and every surface that shows it says so.
_state_doc: Stored, and currently unused: state rules are not built, so answers say
'federal only' whichever state this is. It is filled in because the
onboarding asks for it, and a demo profile with a blank field teaches
that the field does not matter.
_birth_year_doc: Both 63 in 2026, which is the age that makes the IRMAA lesson bite: the
premium surcharge is set by income from TWO YEARS EARLIER, so what this
household does this year decides what it pays at 65. A household already
on Medicare would make the same point less sharply - the decision would
Year, never a date. Every age rule in tax law is annual, so the day and
month buy nothing and are a primary identifier - see the onboarding
design's note on what the profile deliberately does not hold.
_income_doc: Prior-year taxable income. With the 2026 married-joint standard deduction
of 32,200 this puts MAGI at 212,200 against a first IRMAA tier of
218,000 - leaving 5,800 of headroom, against 31,400 to the next ordinary
bracket and 37,800 to the investment surtax.
That ordering is the whole point of the household: the NEAREST tax line
is a cliff, not a slope, and it costs 2,296.80 a year for the couple to
cross by a dollar. gen-demo-household.py asserts the headroom still lands
in range, so an edit here that broke the lesson fails rather than quietly
making the product's own teaching copy wrong.
